scope: Theorem 2.1 (Two-to-one games with imperfect completeness) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of directed feedback vertex set” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-directed-feedback-vertex-set-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 606657a956af61c2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every constant θ ∈ (0, 1/2), there are constant label sets X, Y such that it is NP-hard, by a deterministic polynomial-time reduction, to distinguish two-to-one games of the following kinds: (i) there is a labeling of value at least 1 − θ; (ii) every labeling has value at most θ. Every constraint is a total map X → Y with exactly two preimages of each label in Y . The label sets may depend on θ.
